Dear Subscriber,

Your subscription to Business Weekly will [1] on December 31. To continue receiving the magazine without interruption, please renew before that date. [2] Renewing for two years saves you 25 percent compared with the single-year price. You can renew online at www.businessweekly.example [3] by returning the enclosed form. We [4] our readers' loyalty and look forward to serving you in the coming year.

Customer Service

questions.explanation: A subscription 'expires' on a given date, meaning it ends.

choices: The magazine is printed on recycled paper.
We are offering special rates to our loyal readers.
Our offices are closed on December 25.
The editor will retire next year.
questions.explanation: The sentence introduces the rates discussed in the next sentence.
Two alternatives are offered: renew online or return the form.
After the subject 'We', a conjugated verb is needed.

text:
Study Links Sleep to Workplace Performance

A new study by researchers at Hamilton University suggests that employees who sleep at least seven hours a night are [1] more productive than those who sleep less. The study followed 800 workers over a period of two years. [2] Those who reported poor sleep made [3] errors and missed more deadlines. Experts recommend that companies encourage healthy habits [4] flexible schedules and quiet rest areas.

questions.explanation: An adverb is needed to modify the comparative 'more productive'.

choices: The participants came from a wide range of industries.
Coffee consumption has risen over the past decade.
questions.explanation: The sentence gives details about the study sample, before the results are given.
'More errors' completes the comparison with 'missed more deadlines'.
'Such as' introduces examples.

text:
MEMBERS' NOTICE

The Harmon Art Museum will be [1] to the public on Monday, March 3, for the installation of a new exhibition. Members, [2], will be able to enter between 10 a.m. and noon. [3] Please present your membership card at the entrance. The exhibition, titled Light and Color, [4] more than 80 works from private collections.

questions.explanation: The passive adjective 'closed' is needed after 'will be'.
'However' marks the exception for members as opposed to the public.

choices: Entry for members is free of charge.
questions.explanation: The sentence is about members' entry and precedes the instruction to show the card.
A present-tense verb is needed after 'The exhibition'.

[3] Experience in a fine-dining restaurant is essential, and a culinary diploma is preferred. We offer a competitive salary, free meals, and the opportunity to work in a [4] and creative environment.

questions.explanation: The present continuous 'is seeking' is needed.
A base verb parallel to 'create' and 'ensure' is needed.

choices: The restaurant is located near the harbor.
The role requires strong leadership and the ability to work under pressure.
questions.explanation: The sentence describes the role and precedes the requirements.
An adjective parallel to 'creative' is needed.

text:
Customer (6:30 p.m.): My internet has been very slow since yesterday. [1]
Agent (6:31 p.m.): I'm sorry about that. Let me [2] a test on your line.
Agent (6:34 p.m.): I can see that there is a service problem in your area. Our engineers are [3] on it, and it should be resolved by tomorrow morning. As compensation, we will [4] your next bill by $10.

choices: My landlord is selling the apartment.
I would like to order a new phone.
Your offices are closed on Sundays.

questions.explanation: The customer adds an action already taken, before the agent runs a test.
One 'runs' a test, meaning one performs it.
The present continuous 'are working on it' is needed.
A bill can be 'reduced' by a given amount.

text:
MEMO
To: All staff
From: Human Resources
Subject: Holiday schedule

The office will be closed from December 24 to January 1. [1] Employees who need to work during this period must obtain written approval from their department head [2] December 10. Those who do so will receive a compensation day [3] in January. Please remember to [4] all confidential documents before leaving on December 23.

choices: The cafeteria will be renovated in February.
Parking fees will increase next year.
The holiday party was a great success.
Normal business hours will resume on Monday, January 2.
questions.explanation: The sentence completes the closure information, before the exception for workers.
'By' introduces a deadline.
'Later in January' indicates a time after the closure.
One 'secures' documents, meaning one stores them safely.

text:

Sponsorship packages begin at $1,000, and every package includes [3] entries for your employees. We would be happy to [4] the details with you at your convenience.

choices: Lincoln Park has a new playground.

questions.explanation: The sentence presents the event and leads to last year's results.
An adverb is needed to modify the participle 'displayed'.
An adjective is needed before 'entries'.
After 'would be happy to', the base form is used.

text:
Dear Mr. Silva,

We are writing to confirm that your support request #20418 has been [1]. The problem with your accounting software was caused by an outdated version, which we have now updated remotely. [2] You should be able to log in as usual. If the issue [3], please reply to this e-mail and we will reopen your case. questions.explanation: The passive 'has been resolved' is needed.

choices: No further action is required on your part.
The software is available in three languages.
Our technicians work in teams of four.
The survey results will be published in May.
questions.explanation: The sentence follows the solution and precedes the confirmation that login works.
After 'If the issue', the third-person singular present is needed.
One 'takes' a few minutes to do something.
